about: Unicode text -> Shree-Lipi 7 Bangla bytes (Bengali, Assamese, Manipuri in Bangla script; fonts SHREE-BAN7-xxxx = S<dddd>892.TTF, SHREE-ASS7-xxxx = S<dddd>896.TTF, Shree-Ban7-001/002, Shree-Ass7-001/002), answered by Shree's own composers S8BanU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Ban764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, raw bytes) for the same keystroke. Assamese has no composer of its own: the 15 .ASS keyboards are typed by the same Ban composers (ৰ = code 26, ৱ = code 7C in the shared code table). bytes = the 7 composer's raw output, one hex byte per glyph code. READ counts.fontCheck BEFORE USING THESE BYTES FOR A SHREE-BAN7 FONT: S8Ban764 writes the SHREE-BAN 4/5/6 layout at the family-differing codes - ঃ as 40, the half-ন hook as 96, subscript ্ন as 97, ৺ as A5, ধ্ম as 8C, ব্ঝ as A8, and FF as a zero-width filler - so its answers are right for SHREE-BAN/ASS 4/5/6 fonts (and Shree-Ass7-001/002) but at those codes wrong for SHREE-BAN7/ASS7 (rendered: কঃ draws ক + hook, ন্দ draws ঃদ, — draws -ড়্গ-ড়্গ-); and it writes ব and ৰ as AF and ৱ as A4, which in every installed SHREE-BAN font draw ব্ল and ব (SHREE-ASS fonts: AF = ৱ, B9 = ৰ, A4 = ব). These answers are kept as the composer wrote them (they are what Shree's composer types); counts.fontCheck lists each byte, what it draws per family, and how many truth strings use it. kind: vendor-key = a layer-0 key (or a Ctrl+Space key holding a code >= 80) of one of the 42 shipped keyboards (27 .BAN + 15 .ASS), each loaded from its ORIGINAL path because the composers switch typing mode by keyboard name (PHONETIC/ENG answer a consonant with its hasanta form, INSCRIPT/INDICA/NEWROMA/PHONET86 take the pre-base signs after the letter and answer ে/ৈ as EB/ED); source names the keyboard, key and the internal codes the key holds. Ctrl+Space keys holding a code under 80 and all Ctrl+Shift+1 keys are left out: S8Ban764 answers them as other keys (a Ctrl+Space code c < 80 as the layer-0 key chr(c), every Ctrl+Shift+1 key as its layer-0 key) while S8BanU64 answers the code, so those pairs are misaligned (every code is probed on layer 0 instead). canonical = probe in Shree's typing order for Bangla: the pre-base signs ি ে ৈ struck FIRST, ো = ে + letter + া, ৌ = ে + letter + ৗ, the reph (code 40) struck AFTER the letter and its signs, ra-phala = code D1, ya-phala = code D2, conjuncts through the Link code 64; canonical:ligature-code = a letter typed with its own code (ক্ষ 5C, ড় 45, ঢ় 41, য় D7, জ় 23), preferred; canonical:pending-link = sequence ending in a Link (the composer answers the hasanta form it is waiting with); e/ai-sign code EB/E5 (the other e/ai glyphs EB/ED), reph-then-anusvara/candrabindu and anusvara/candrabindu/visarga-then-reph = other accepted orders; alt:* = the composer answer for a non-canonical typing order or a visibly different form (reph struck first, র + Link + letter = র with a visible hasanta, reph before a post-base sign, C + Link + র / য = visible hasanta + full letter instead of the ra-/ya-phala, a pre-base sign struck after the letter) - kept, not used as truth; quirk:* = the Unicode composer wrote something other than the codes mean (it drops the ya-phala under a reph, and letters after ক্ষ/জ় + reph), or the 7 composer silently dropped a code the Unicode composer wrote (nukta F0 - it has no nukta, only the precomposed ড় ঢ় য় জ় codes draw one; ৄ ৢ ৣ ৠ ৡ; ো/ৌ typed as E2/E3 after a letter; ং or ঃ struck before the reph; the reph when ঁ is struck after ী + reph), or wrote a stand-in (₹ as 3C, no glyph) - kept for evidence, not used. Assamese: counts.assamese; what could not be probed: counts.notProbed. Unicode keys are what the Unicode composer wrote, except that ো / ৌ typed in Shree's order come back decomposed (U+09C7 U+09BE / U+09C7 U+09D7) and are filed under the precomposed U+09CB / U+09CC that normal (NFC) text holds; ড় ঢ় য় come back precomposed (U+09DC U+09DD U+09DF), জ় as U+099C U+09BC. Conjuncts with no ligature in the font come back as letter + visible hasanta F4 + letter (there are no half forms). The composer's rules with examples: ban7-patterns.txt.

fontCheck.method: every byte the composer writes was looked up in the cmaps of SHREE-BAN7-0550/0592/0597 (S0xxx892), SHREE-ASS7-0550 (S0550896), Shree-Ban7-001 (WBAN7001), Shree-Ass7-001 (WASS7001), SHREE-BAN-0550 and SHREE-ASS-0550 (S05500F2/F6, 4/5/6) and answers were rendered in them (tsk-ban/pics). Only the bytes below differ between the families or draw another letter; the 7 composer never writes 08 09 0A 0B-0F 1A-1F.

8C.ban7: ব (a copy; no ধ্ম glyph in 7)

A8.ban7: দ (a copy; no ব্ঝ glyph in 7)

FF.composerMeans: zero-width filler between two glyphs that do not join (দ্গ = 83 FF 4B, ব্ব = A4 FF A4, — = 2D FF 2D FF 2D)

AF.composerMeans: ব (code 71) and ৰ (code 26), standalone and before signs
AF.note: ব is drawn by A4 in every installed SHREE-BAN/ASS font (and 8C in 7, 08 in 4/5/6); the composer itself writes A4 for ব inside ব্ব (A4 FF A4) and ব্ল (A4 C3)

A4.composerMeans: ৱ (code 7C) when standalone; ব inside ব্ব / ব্ল
A4.note: no SHREE-BAN font has ৱ; SHREE-ASS fonts draw ৱ at AF and ৰ at B9 (the র code)

fontCheck.summary: S8Ban764 writes the SHREE-BAN 4/5/6 code layout at the family-differing codes (40 ঃ, 96 hook, 97 ্ন, A5 ৺, 8C ধ্ম, A8 ব্ঝ, FF filler): its answers draw right in SHREE-BAN-xxxx / SHREE-ASS-xxxx (4/5/6) and in Shree-Ass7-001/002, and wrong in SHREE-BAN7-xxxx, SHREE-ASS7-xxxx (S0xxx896) and Shree-Ban7-001/002 at exactly those codes (for those fonts: swap 40<->96 and 97<->A5, drop FF; 8C/A8 have no 7 glyph). Separately it writes ব and ৰ as AF and ৱ as A4, which draw ব্ল/ৱ and ব in every installed font.
fontCheck.familyDifferingCodesSummary: emitted: 25 40 96 97 A5 8C A8 FF; never emitted: 08 09 0A 0B 0C 0D 0E 0F 1A 1B 1C 1D 1E 1F. The emitted ones are used with their 4/5/6 meaning (40 ঃ, 96 half-ন hook, 97 ্ন, A5 ৺, 8C ধ্ম, A8 ব্ঝ, FF zero-width filler; 25 only for % itself).

assamese.composer: C:/Shree-Lipi nxt has no S8Ass*.dll: the 15 .ASS keyboards (13 *.ASS + MODBAN.ass, NEWROMA.ass) are typed by S8BanU64/S8Ban764, whose code table holds ৰ = code 26 and ৱ = code 7C next to the Bengali letters. Every code typed on both an .ASS and a .BAN keyboard (188) gets the same 7 bytes, except 4 that differ only by the phonetic/inscript typing mode of the keyboard, not by .ASS (fin2: vendor-row comparison). The Unicode composer answers the ra key of the .ASS keyboards with Bengali র U+09B0 (7: B9), code 26 with ৰ U+09F0 (7: AF).
assamese.fonts: fc cmp S0550892.TTF (SHREE-BAN7-0550) vs S0550896.TTF (SHREE-ASS7-0550): 212 of 218 codes identical in outline and advance; differing: AF (BAN7 ব্ল, ASS7 ৱ = BAN7 glyph 9E), B9 (BAN7 র, ASS7 ৰ), and 25, 3A, 8D (ব্ড), 9E (ৱ) present in BAN7 only. Shree-Ban7-001 vs Shree-Ass7-001 (WBAN7001/WASS7001) differ in 34 codes: digits 30-39 redrawn, 40<->96 and 97<->A5 swapped (WASS7001 has the 4/5/6 order), AF ৱ, B9 ৰ, 8D/9E absent (fin2/cmp-*.txt, fin2/rows-ass.png).
assamese.verdict: No separate ass7-groundtruth.json: the composers and their bytes are the same for Assamese, so these pairs are the Assamese truth too (Assamese strings with ৰ ৱ are in it). What an ASS7 font does with them: B9 (written for র) draws ৰ, AF (written for ব and ৰ) draws ৱ, A4 (written for ৱ) draws ব - so in an ASS7 font the composer bytes give ৰ for typed র but ৱ for ব/ৰ and ব for ৱ.

counts.notProbed: Sequences longer than 4 codes cannot be typed with one key (a conjunct slot holds at most 4 codes; a slot reference B0-CF/90-9F inside a slot is ignored - tested, fin2-nesttest.js), so C1্C2্C3 clusters whose third letter is not র/য (ত্ত্ব জ্জ্ব ন্ত্ব ন্দ্ব) and a 2-consonant cluster with a vowel sign AND a reph or a phala are not in the truth. 3-consonant clusters that fit are: C্C + ra-/ya-phala (ন্ত্র স্ত্র ন্ধ্য), ক্ষ (own code) with a letter (ক্ষ্ম ঙ্ক্ষ), reph + C্C (র্ত্ত), and C্C্ pending.
